articleTitle: 1ERRATUM
TAUER MASAS IN THE HYPERFINITE II1 FACTOR
abstract: A Tauer masa in ℛ is obtained by taking an increasing sequence of type I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> subfactors generating ℛ and masas in each subfactor which form an increasing chain. We show that the Tauer masas have Pukánszky invariant {1} and that the concepts of singularity and strong singularity and the weak asymptotic homomorphism property are equivalent for these masas.

articleTitle: ELEMENTS OF HIGH ORDER IN THE HOMOTOPY GROUPS OF HYPERBOLIC SPACES AT LARGE PRIMES
abstract: It is shown that rationally hyperbolic spaces do not admit a homotopy exponent for their homotopy groups at almost all primes.

articleTitle: INDECOMPOSABILITY OF POLYNOMIALS AND RELATED DIOPHANTINE EQUATIONS
abstract: We present a new criterion for indecomposability of polynomials over ℤ. Using the criterion, we obtain general finiteness result on the polynomial Diophantine equation f(x) = g(y).

articleTitle: A LOCALLY FINITE VARIETY OF RINGS WITH AN UNDECIDABLE EQUATIONAL THEORY
abstract: We prove that the non-finitely based system of polynomial identities over an arbitrary field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{F}}$</tex> of characteristic 2 given by Gupta and Krasilnikov in [A non-finitely based system of polynomial identities which contains the identity x<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> = 0, Quart. J. Math. 53 (2002), 173–183] can, by a slight modification, be turned into an independent system. This has important consequences for algorithmic problems in algebra: there is a locally finite-dimensional variety of associative algebras (and, in particular, a locally finite variety of rings) that has an undecidable equational theory. For such a variety, the uniform word problem is unsolvable, and yet the word problem is recursively solvable for each individual finitely presented algebra (ring) in that variety.

articleTitle: GROUP-GRADED ALGEBRAS AND THE RELATIVE PROJECTIVITY OF POINTED GROUPS
abstract: We interpret pointed groups over a G-algebra as isomorphism classes of bimodules over interior G-algebras with a graded structure. We characterize the relative projectivity of pointed groups in these terms. As an application, we give a group-graded algebra theoretic proof of a result of Fan, Puig and Zhou (J. Algebra 2001).

articleTitle: CANCELLATIVITY IS UNDECIDABLE FOR AUTOMATIC SEMIGROUPS
abstract: Via an encoding of the Modified Post's Correspondence Problem, this paper shows that it is undecidable whether an automatic semigroup is cancellative.

articleTitle: FERMAT COVERS, FERMAT HYPERSURFACES AND ABELIAN VARIETIES OF FERMAT TYPE
abstract: Albanese maps for smooth projective models of a class of Abelian covers of projective space branched along particular hyperplane arrangements are studied. In some cases it is shown that the image of the Albanese map gives a cycle in the Albanese variety which is not numerically equivalent to a linear combination of intersections of divisors. Smooth projective varieties with this property are said to be Albanese exotic. Few concrete examples of such varieties are known.

articleTitle: LAX CONSTRAINTS IN SEMISIMPLE LIE GROUPS
abstract: Instead of studying Lax equations as such, a solution Z of a Lax equation is assumed to be given. Then Z is regarded as defining a constraint on a non-autonomous linear differential equation associated with the Lax equation. In generic cases, quadrature and sometimes algebraic formulae in terms of Z are then proved for solution x of the linear differential equation, and examples are given where these formulae lead to new results in higher-order variational problems for curves in general semisimple Lie groups G, extending results previously obtained by different methods for the case where G has dimension 3. The new construction is explored in detail for G = SU(m).

articleTitle: COMPRESSIONS, CONVEX GEOMETRY AND THE FREIMAN–BILU THEOREM
abstract: We note a link between combinatorial results of Bollobás and Leader concerning sumsets in the grid, the Brunn–Minkowski theorem and a result of Freiman and Bilu concerning the structure of sets A ⊆ ℤ with small doubling. Our main result is the following. If ε > 0 and if A is a finite non-empty subset of a torsion-free abelian group with |A + A| ≤ K|A|, then A may be covered by e<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">O(1)</sup> progressions of dimension ⌊ log <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> K + ε ⌋ and size at most |A|.

articleTitle: THOMAS'S FAMILY OF THUE EQUATIONS OVER FUNCTION FIELDS
abstract: We consider a function field analogue of Thomas's family of Thue equations X<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> − (λ − 1)X<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>Y − (λ + 2)X Y<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> − Y<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> = ξ, where the solutions X,Y come from the ring C[T], the parameter λ ∈ C[T] is some non-constant polynomial and 0 ≠ ξ ∈ C. In this paper we solve this family completely.

articleTitle: POSITIVE QUATERNION-KÄHLER 16-MANIFOLDS WITH b2 = 0
abstract: It is known that if the second Betti number of a 4n-dimensional positive quaterion-Kähler manifold M satisfies b<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(M) ≥ 1, then M is homothetic to the complex Grassmannian <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{G}{\rm r}_2(\mathbb{C}^{n+2})$</tex>. In sixteen dimensions, it is also known that if b<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>(M) = 1, then M is homothetic to the quaternionic projective space ℍℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>. Here, we prove that the fourth Betti number of a positive quaternion-Kähler 16-manifold is at least 3 if b<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(M) = 0. We also explore the consequences of other restrictions suggested by the vanishing of certain indices of twisted Dirac operators on the Wolf spaces.

articleTitle: TWO ORBITAL EQUATIONS IN PRIMITIVE PERMUTATION GROUPS
abstract: The orbit and orbital are basis concepts in group theory. Peter M. Neumann began to investigate the orbital equations in [3] and gave two orbital equations to be solved. The purpose of this article is to interpret the solutions to the two porbital equations: Γ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup> = Γ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> and Γ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> = Γ∪ Γ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>, where n≥ 3

articleTitle: ON TORSION-FREE CRAWLEY GROUPS
abstract: The notion of a Crawley p-group is well known in Abelian group theory. In this present work, a corresponding concept is introduced for torsion-free groups. The principal result, which uses the set-theoretic notions of the diamond and Martin’s axiom, establishes an independence result for ℵ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-free Crawley groups.

articleTitle: CARTAN DETERMINANTS OF CELLULAR ALGEBRAS
abstract: Let A be a finite-dimensional cellular algebra over a field. It is shown that the Cartan determinant of A is a positive integer; furthermore, the Cartan determinant of value 1 is equivalent to the condition that A is quasi-hereditary. In this article, we establish a formula for expressing the Cartan determinants of cellular algebras. By applying this formula, we obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for a cellular algebra with Cartan determinant 2 to be standardly stratified. Moreover, we provide a sufficient condition for an arbitrary cellular algebra to be standardly stratified and an inductive construction of standardly stratified cellular algebras.

articleTitle: UNIVERSAL SPACES OF TWO-CELL COMPLEXES AND THEIR EXPONENT BOUNDS
abstract: Let P<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n+1</sup> be a two-cell complex which is formed by attaching a (2n + 1)-cell to a 2m-sphere by a suspension map. We construct a universal space U for P<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n+1</sup> in the category of homotopy associative, homotopy commutative H-spaces. By universal, we mean that U is homotopy associative, homotopy commutative and has the property that any map f: P<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n+1</sup> → Y to a homotopy associative, homotopy commutative H-space Y extends to a uniquely determined H-map f̄: U → Y. We then prove upper and lower bounds of the H-homotopy exponent of U. In the case of a mod p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sup>, Moore space U is the homotopy fibre S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n+1</sup>{p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sup>} of the p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sup>-power map on S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n+1</sup>, and we reproduce Neisendorfer's result that S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n+1</sup>{p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sup>} is homotopy associative, homotopy commutative and that the p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sup>-power map on S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n+1</sup>{p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sup>} is null homotopic.

articleTitle: ON MINIMAL SURFACES WHOSE GAUSS MAP IS INVARIANT BY A HOLOMORPHIC FOLIATION
abstract: We study real minimal surfaces ψ: M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> ↪ ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> under the hypothesis that the holomorphic Gauss map of the immersion is invariant by a holomorphic foliation with singularities. We give a sort of Huber–Osserman theorem regarding the algebraicity of the holomorphic Gauss map.

articleTitle: ON THE LEAST n WITH χ(n) ≠ 1
abstract: Suppose that a > 1. By using a method of Linnik employing his Large Sieve one may derive the following result. The number of primitive Dirichlet characters χ with conductor ≤Q such that χ(n) = 1 for all n ≤ (log Q)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</sup> is O(Q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2/a+ε</sup>). We improve the exponent 2/a for a > 2 by using a refined version by Heath-Brown of the Halasz–Montgomery ‘Large Values method’.

articleTitle: VECTOR BUNDLES ON CURVES ADMITTING A CONNECTION
abstract: Let k be any infinite perfect field. Let E be a vector bundle over a smooth projective curve defined over k. We prove that E admits a connection if the degree of every indecomposable component of E is zero. This has been proved (when k = ℂ) in M. F. Atiyah [2] and A. Weil [7].

articleTitle: ON A BREŠAR–ŠEMRL CONJECTURE AND DERIVATIONS OF BANACH ALGEBRAS
abstract: In this paper, we answer a question on derivations of dense algebras of linear operators posed by Brešar and šemrl. Our theorem implies the following result: let ℬ be a complex Banach algebra, and let d and g be continuous derivations of ℬ. If dg(x) is quasi-nilpotent for every x ∈ ℬ, then dg(x)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> lies in the radical of ℬ for every x ∈ ℬ. This result was proved by Brešar and Šemrl with the additional assumption gd = dg.

articleTitle: A SaitÔ–Tomita–Lusin Theorem for JB*-Triples and Applications
abstract: A theorem of Lusin is proved in the non-ordered context of JB*-triples. This is applied to obtain versions of a general transitivity theorem and to deduce refinements of facial structure in closed unit ballls of JB*-triples and duals.

articleTitle: ORBITAL EQUATIONS IN PRIMITIVE PERMUTATION GROUPS
LIPSCHITZ FUNCTIONS ON HERMITIAN BANACH *-ALGEBRAS
abstract: We characterize semisimple Hermitian Banach *-algebras <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{A}$</tex> with ‘rich’ spaces of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{A}$</tex>-Lipschitz functions and describe these spaces. For unital algebras <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{A}$</tex>, the presence of a nonlinear <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{A}$</tex>-Lipschitz function implies that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{A}$</tex> is a C*-algebra. If <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{A}$</tex> only has finite-dimensional irreducible representations and their dimensions are bounded, then the space of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{A}$</tex>-Lipschitz functions coincides with the space of all Lipschitz (in the usual sense) functions. If these dimensions are unbounded or if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{A}$</tex> has an infinite-dimensional irreducible representation, then the space of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{A}$</tex>-Lipschitz functions coincides with the space of all operator Lipschitz functions.The non-unital case is more varied. There is a large class of non-C*-equivalent algebras <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{A}$</tex> whose spaces of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{A}$</tex>-Lipschitz functions contain all functions g with Fourier transform <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \widehat{g}$</tex> satisfying <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\int_{\mathbb{R}}\left| t\widehat{g}(t)\right|\rm{d} t<\infty $</tex>. These algebras are defined by a very mild condition: the function g(t) = t<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{A}$</tex>-Lipschitz function. They are isomorphic to symmetrically normed Jordan ideals of C*-algebras. If the completion of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{A}$</tex> in the Ptak–Rajkov C*-norm is not a CCR-algebra, then all <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{A}$</tex>-Lipschitz functions are operator Lipschitz functions.

articleTitle: VARIATIONS ON BELYI'S THEOREM
abstract: We establish a simple criterion for a variety to be defined over a number field, which allows us to extend to higher dimension several known results relative to the field of definition of complex curves as well as providing some new results in dimension one.

articleTitle: NOTE ON CROSSING CHANGES
abstract: For any pair of knots of Gordian distance two, we construct an infinite family of knots which are ‘between’ these two knots, that is, which differ from the given two knots by one crossing change. In particular, we prove that every knot of unknotting number two can be unknotted via infinitely many different knots of unknotting number one.

articleTitle: VITALI–HAHN–SAKS THEOREM FOR VECTOR MEASURES ON OPERATOR ALGEBRAS
abstract: We show that the direct generalization of the Vitali–Hahn–Saks theorem is not valid for all measures on von Neumann algebras. By applying a general equicontinuity argument, we prove a direct extension of the Vitali–Hahn–Saks theorem for a wide range of vector measures on von Neumann algebra s and JBW algebras. We also characterize relatively compact sets of vector measures on operator algebras.

articleTitle: ON THE LEGACY OF FREE DIVISORS III: FUNCTIONS AND DIVISORS ON COMPLETE INTERSECTIONS
REPRESENTATION TYPE OF ∞λℋ1μ
abstract: For a semi-simple finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal g}$</tex>, we classify the representation type of the associative algebras associated with the categories <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ {{\infty_\lambda}{H}_\mu^1}$</tex> of Harish–Chandra bimodules for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\cal g}$</tex>.

articleTitle: DESINGULARIZATIONS OF CALABI–YAU 3-FOLDS WITH A CONICAL SINGULARITY
abstract: We study Calabi–Yau 3-folds M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> with a conical singularity x modelled on a Calabi–Yau cone V. We construct desingularizations of M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, obtaining a 1-parameter family of compact, non-singular Calabi–Yau 3-folds which has M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> as the limit. The way we do so is to choose an asymptotically conical Calabi–Yau 3-fold Y modelled on the same cone V, and then glue into M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> at x after applying a homothety to Y. We then get a 1-parameter family of nearly Calabi–Yau 3-folds M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf> depending on a small real variable t. For sufficiently small t, we show that the nearly Calabi–Yau structures on M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf> can be deformed to genuine Calabi–Yau structures, thereby obtaining the desingularizations of M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. Our result can be applied to resolving orbifold singularities and hence will provide a quantitative description of the Calabi–Yau metrics on the crepant resolutions.

articleTitle: THE DISTRIBUTION OF LATTICE POINTS IN ELLIPTIC ANNULI
abstract: We study the distribution of the number of lattice points lying in thin elliptical annuli. It has been conjectured by Bleher and Lebowitz that if the width of the annuli tends to zero and their area tends to infinity, then the distribution of this number, normalized to have zero mean and unit variance, is Gaussian. This has been proved by Hughes and Rudnick for circular annuli whose width shrinks to zero sufficiently slowly. We prove this conjecture for ellipses whose aspect ratio is transcendental and strongly Diophantine, also assuming the width shrinks slowly to zero.

articleTitle: On the Manifold of Complemented Principal Inner Ideals in JB*-Triples
abstract: The set 필 of Neher's classes of tripotents in an arbitrary JB*-triple Z is considered and a natural complex-analytic Banach manifold structure is defined on it. The relationship between 필 and the Grassmann manifold of all complemented principal inner ideals in Z is studied in detail, and the smooth complete vector fields on 필 are characterized as smooth complete equivariant vector fields on the manifold M of tripotents of Z.

articleTitle: EQUIVARIANT HARMONIC CYLINDERS
abstract: We prove that a primitive harmonic map is equivariant if and only if it admits a holomorphic potential of degree one. We investigate when the equivariant harmonic map is periodic and, as an application, discuss constant mean curvature cylinders with screw motion symmetries.

articleTitle: LIE G-TORI OF SYMPLECTIC TYPE
abstract: We classify centreless Lie G-tori of type C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> including the most difficult case r = 2 by applying techniques due to Seligman. In particular, we show that the coordinate algebra of a Lie G-torus of type C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is either an associative G-torus with involution or a Clifford G-torus. Our results generalize the classification of the core of the extended affine Lie algebras of type C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> by Allison and Gao.

articleTitle: TWISTORIAL HARMONIC MORPHISMS WITH ONE-DIMENSIONAL FIBRES ON SELF-DUAL FOUR-MANIFOLDS
abstract: We introduce a general notion of twistorial map and classify twistorial harmonic morphisms with one-dimensional fibres from self-dual four-manifolds. Such maps can be characterized as those that pull back Abelian monopoles to self-dual connections. In fact, the constructions involve solving a generalized monopole equation, and also the Beltrami fields equation of hydrodynamics, and lead to constructions of self-dual metrics.

articleTitle: COMBABLE GROUPS HAVE GROUP COHOMOLOGY OF POLYNOMIAL GROWTH
abstract: Group cohomology of polynomial growth is defined for any finitely generated discrete group, using cochains that have polynomial growth with respect to the word length function. We give a geometric condition that guarantees that it agrees with the usual group cohomology and verify this condition for a class of combable groups. Our condition involves a chain complex that is closely related to exotic cohomology theories studied by Allcock and Gersten and by Mineyev.

articleTitle: AUTOMORPHISM FIXED POINTS IN THE MODULI SPACE OF SEMI-STABLE BUNDLES
abstract: Given an automorphism τ of a smooth complex algebraic curve X, there is an induced action of the finite group G generated by τ on the moduli space \mathscr{M} of semi-stable rank-2 holomorphic bundles of fixed degree. We give a complete description of the fixed variety in terms of moduli spaces of parabolic bundles with flags and weights at the special orbits on the quotient curve X/G.
